title: Rational Hopf modules and their symmetric and finite free dual coactions over a ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $C$ a commutative Hopf $A$-algebra, with comultiplication $\Delta$, counit $\epsilon$, and antipode $S$. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For an $A$-module $M$, a rational right coaction is an $A$-linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_A C$ with $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_M$ and $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$, under the tensor unit and associativity identifications. Write $\operatorname{Sym}_A M$ and $\iota_M$ for [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Its degree-$n$ submodule is $(\operatorname{im}\iota_M)^n$, equivalently the span of all products of $n$ linear generators as in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. For any linear map $r:M\to M\otimes_A C$, the induced symmetric map is the algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}_A M\to\operatorname{Sym}_A M\otimes_A C$ extending $(\iota_M\otimes1)r$. When $A$ is nonzero and $M$ is finite free, its contragredient coaction on $M^\vee$ is the linear map determined in any finite basis $e_i$, with dual basis $e^i$, by $e^i\mapsto\sum_j e^j\otimes S(c_{ij})$, where $\rho(e_j)=\sum_i e_i\otimes c_{ij}$. Use Mathlib's chosen finite basis to construct this map, rather than choosing unspecified data.
